credibility_rationale: Official legislative text from the Library of Congress.

headline: Congress to continue funding Voice of America, despite Trump's wishes
summary: A bipartisan FY2026 appropriations bill allocated roughly $650 million to USAGM, well above the roughly $150 million the administration had requested, rejecting the push to defund or disestablish the agency.
credibility_rationale: Specialized broadcast-industry trade press reporting on legislative text.

headline: Judge says Kari Lake unlawfully ran USAGM, voids Voice of America layoffs
summary: A federal judge ruled that Kari Lake's leadership of USAGM was unlawful and voided VOA layoffs conducted under a deferred-resignation program, a further legal setback for the administration's effort to shrink the agency.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Trump Administration Deals Potentially Fatal Blow to National Climate Assessment
source: Columbia Law School Climate Change Law Sabin Center
summary: The administration cut funding for the U.S. Global Change Research Program and dismissed roughly 400 scientists working on the Sixth National Climate Assessment in April 2025.
credibility_rationale: Academic legal research center with editorial review, though focused on climate-law advocacy topics.

headline: U.S. Global Change Research Program (USGCRP): Overview and Considerations for Congress
summary: CRS confirmed NCA6 authors were dismissed and program funding cut in 2025, with the statutory 2027 assessment deadline now uncertain, rather than being addressed via a dedicated restructuring executive order.
credibility_rationale: Official nonpartisan congressional research product.

headline: Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding and Motor Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards Under the Clean Air Act
summary: EPA published a final rule rescinding the 2009 endangerment finding and the associated motor-vehicle greenhouse gas emission standards under the Clean Air Act.
credibility_rationale: Official federal rulemaking document.

headline: Up in the Air: EPA Opens Comment on Repealing Endangerment Finding, Motor Vehicle GHG Rules
summary: EPA proposed repealing greenhouse gas emissions standards for vehicles and rescinding the 2009 endangerment finding, opening a public comment period ahead of the 2026 final rule.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client-alert analysis of the agency's own proposed rule.

headline: EPA & Army Corps Unveil Clear, Durable WOTUS Proposal
summary: EPA and the Army Corps of Engineers proposed a new 'waters of the United States' rule narrowing federal Clean Water Act jurisdiction to relatively permanent waters and adjacent wetlands, consistent with the Supreme Court's Sackett decision.
credibility_rationale: Official EPA press release describing the agency's own proposed rule.

headline: Trump Rescinds California's Emission Waivers: What It Means for the Future of EV Mandates
summary: Trump signed three Congressional Review Act resolutions revoking EPA Clean Air Act waivers that let California set its own vehicle-emissions and EV-sales-mandate rules; eleven states sued to block the rescissions.
credibility_rationale: Law firm analysis summarizing signed legislation and resulting litigation.

headline: EPA Will Retain PFOA and PFOS CERCLA Hazardous Substance Designation
summary: EPA announced it will retain, rather than revisit, the CERCLA hazardous-substance designation for PFOA/PFOS, while planning a broader framework rule to guide future PFAS designations.
credibility_rationale: Legal trade publication summarizing EPA's announced decision.

headline: EPA Eliminates Environmental Justice Offices Under Trump
summary: EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin ordered the closure of the stand-alone Office of Environmental Justice and External Civil Rights and its regional divisions, citing the administration's anti-DEI executive order.
credibility_rationale: Nonprofit news outlet reporting corroborated by EPA's own statements.

headline: RFK Jr. Plans to Slash HHS Workforce by 25% in Massive Reorganization
summary: HHS announced a restructuring consolidating 28 divisions into 15, including folding several CDC functions such as HIV and maternal-child health into a new Administration for a Healthy America.
credibility_rationale: Health-policy trade outlet with editorial standards, based on HHS's own announcement.

headline: Court Halts RFK Health Agency Restructuring
summary: A federal court blocked parts of the HHS reorganization from proceeding, though thousands of mass layoffs already underway were allowed to stand.
credibility_rationale: Mainstream news outlet report on a litigation outcome.

headline: FDA to Conduct Safety Review of Abortion Pill Mifepristone
summary: FDA launched a retrospective safety review of mifepristone at HHS Secretary Kennedy's direction that could lead to tighter telehealth/mail-order restrictions or removal of the drug from the market.
credibility_rationale: National political news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Abortion Pill Mifepristone Access Steady Under Trump, FDA Review Looms
summary: A federal court in Virginia ruled that FDA's existing mifepristone restrictions were 'arbitrary and capricious' and ordered the agency to reconsider them, even as a separate administration safety review remained pending.
credibility_rationale: Wire-adjacent business news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: CMS Rescinds Post-Dobbs EMTALA Guidance, Raising New Questions for Emergency Departments
summary: CMS formally rescinded 2022 guidance stating EMTALA requires hospitals to perform emergency abortions when necessary to stabilize a patient, while maintaining that EMTALA still preempts directly conflicting state bans.
credibility_rationale: Law firm alert summarizing official CMS action.

headline: US Head Start Preschool Programs Hit by Trump Cuts, Funding Delays
summary: The administration proposed eliminating Head Start funding in an internal draft budget and separately delayed and withheld grant funding, though the final budget sent to Congress did not include full elimination.
credibility_rationale: National news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: NEW: Trump Admin Withholding Nearly $1 Billion in Funding for Head Start
summary: A Senate Democratic office reported the administration withheld close to $1 billion in Head Start grants, citing a 37% year-over-year decline in funding issued to centers nationwide.
credibility_rationale: Partisan congressional office press release, not independent reporting.

headline: HHS Shifts Title X Grants Focus Away from Planned Parenthood
summary: HHS issued new 2027 Title X funding guidelines requiring grantees not to perform or refer for abortions, though the administration has not formally reinstated the 2019 'Protect Life Rule' despite Secretary Kennedy's stated intent to do so.
credibility_rationale: Ideologically-leaning but editorially staffed national outlet.

headline: First Circuit Reverses Block on Trump's Planned Parenthood Funding Cuts
summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act's one-year Medicaid defunding of Planned Parenthood took partial effect after litigation; a district court injunction blocking it was reversed on appeal before the provision expired in July 2026.
credibility_rationale: Legal-affairs wire service covering court filings and rulings directly.

headline: A Closer Look at the Work Requirement Provisions in the 2025 Federal Budget Reconciliation Law
summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act, signed July 4, 2025, requires most states to condition Medicaid expansion eligibility on at least 80 hours per month of work or other qualifying activity, phasing in through January 2027.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan health policy research organization.

headline: Mintz IRA Update — Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program Updates for Q3 2025
summary: Rather than repealing the IRA's Medicare drug price negotiation program, the administration continued implementing and expanding it (including into Part B) while narrowing its orphan-drug exclusion, contrary to the recommendation to repeal it.
credibility_rationale: Law firm regulatory update tracking program implementation.

headline: Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing; Withdrawal
summary: HUD formally withdrew the Biden-era 2023 proposed Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing rule, ending that rulemaking process and later replacing it with a minimal certification standard.
credibility_rationale: Official federal rulemaking notice.

headline: HUD Reintroduces Proposed Rule Targeting Rental Aid for Mixed-Status Immigrant Households
summary: HUD proposed a rule requiring verification of citizenship or eligible immigration status for all members of households receiving federal rental assistance, which advocates estimate could affect roughly 80,000 people including 37,000 children.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan state-policy news service.

headline: Interior Department Announces New Arctic Refuge Oil and Gas Lease Sale for January
summary: Interior held a congressionally mandated ANWR Coastal Plain lease sale in January 2025 that drew no bids, the second such sale to fail to attract industry interest since 2021; a further sale was planned under the 2025 reconciliation law.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan budget watchdog group tracking federal leasing data.

headline: Trump Reduces Size of Two National Monuments in Utah as Republicans Reshape Land Management
summary: Trump signed proclamations shrinking Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante national monuments by about 90%, reviving a first-term reduction Biden had reversed; his legal authority to shrink (rather than create) monuments remains legally contested.
credibility_rationale: Major broadcast news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: The Department of the Interior Moves to Restore Coal Industry
summary: Interior terminated the Biden-era programmatic environmental review that had paused coal leasing and restarted the federal coal leasing program, later expanding to roughly 13.1 million acres under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
credibility_rationale: Official agency press release describing its own action.

headline: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Announces It Will Not Develop a Recovery Plan for the Gray Wolf
summary: FWS found that continued Endangered Species Act listing of the gray wolf is 'no longer appropriate' and declined to write a national recovery plan, though full delisting still requires further rulemaking not finalized as of mid-2026.
credibility_rationale: County government association reporting on federal agency action.

headline: Feds Transfer Grizzly Bear Management to States
summary: Interior proposed shifting grizzly bear management authority in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem to Idaho, Wyoming, Montana and Washington without fully delisting the species, after delaying a final delisting rule to December 2026.
credibility_rationale: Nonprofit regional newsroom with editorial standards.

headline: Could Colorado Be Home to the BLM's National Headquarters — Again?
summary: Congressional Republicans introduced legislation to relocate BLM headquarters from Washington back to Grand Junction, Colorado, reviving the first-term Trump move Biden had reversed; as of mid-2026 the relocation had not been completed.
credibility_rationale: Public radio news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Interior Launches Expansive 11th National Offshore Leasing Program to Advance U.S. Energy Dominance
summary: BOEM released a draft 2026-2031 outer continental shelf oil and gas leasing program proposing up to 34 lease sales, including new areas off California, New England and the Carolinas; the program remained unfinalized as of mid-2026.
credibility_rationale: Official agency press release on its own proposed program.

headline: Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce
summary: Trump signed Executive Order 14171 reinstating the Schedule F framework (renamed 'Schedule Policy/Career'), making it easier to reclassify and remove career civil servants in policy-influencing roles across agencies including Interior.
credibility_rationale: Official text of the executive order.

headline: Rescission of Executive Order 11246 Implementing Regulations
summary: DOL published a proposed rule formally rescinding regulations implementing Executive Order 11246 after Trump revoked the 1965 order in January 2025, eliminating OFCCP's core affirmative-action enforcement authority over federal contractors.
credibility_rationale: Official federal rulemaking notice.

headline: DOL Moves to Loosen Independent Contractor Regulations
summary: DOL proposed rescinding the 2024 independent-contractor rule and returning to a Trump-era 'economic reality test,' publishing the proposal for public comment through late April 2026.
credibility_rationale: HR-industry trade press with editorial standards.

headline: Trump Executive Order Seeks to Eliminate Disparate-Impact Liability
summary: Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to deprioritize enforcement actions relying on disparate-impact theories of discrimination and to review regulations imposing such liability under Title VII.
credibility_rationale: Law firm analysis of the executive order's text and directives.

headline: Federal Civil Rights Agency Moves to Stop Requiring Demographic Data Collection After 60 Years
summary: The EEOC voted 2-1 to propose ending mandatory EEO-1 reporting of employee race and sex data by companies with 100 or more employees, opening the rule for public comment.
credibility_rationale: Public broadcaster with established editorial standards.

headline: Rising Agricultural Wages: Context for Congressional Interest in the H-2A Visa Program
summary: Congress has not capped or phased down the H-2A program as recommended; usage instead grew to nearly 400,000 workers in 2025, with pending bipartisan legislation (Farm Workforce Modernization Act) moving in the opposite direction.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan congressional research service report.

headline: Department of Transportation Proposes Dramatic Rollback of Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) Standards
summary: NHTSA proposed resetting CAFE baselines and slowing required fuel-economy increases for model years 2022-2031, projecting a fleet average of about 34.5 mpg by 2031, well below current-law targets; the rule remained a proposal pending comment.
credibility_rationale: Law firm regulatory alert summarizing the proposed rule's text.

headline: As Trump Slashed Weather Agency, His Appointees Have Ties to Companies That Stand to Benefit from Privatizing Forecasts
summary: NOAA cut hundreds of staff, including hurricane hunters and severe-storm researchers, while administration officials with ties to private weather-forecasting firms pushed to commercialize National Weather Service operations; full dismantlement or commercialization has not occurred.
credibility_rationale: Public broadcaster investigative reporting with editorial standards.

headline: Trump Officials Push Citizenship Question in Test Survey for 2030 Census
summary: The Census Bureau is testing a citizenship question ahead of the 2030 census through a 2026 operational field test, after Trump directed Commerce in August 2025 to develop a census excluding unauthorized immigrants from apportionment counts; no final decision on the 2030 questionnaire has been made.
credibility_rationale: National news outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Trump Administration Officially Ends Veteran Abortion Access
summary: Following Justice Department guidance, the VA ended its 2022 policy that had allowed abortion counseling and, in limited cases, abortion care for veterans and dependents.
credibility_rationale: Nonprofit state-focused news network with editorial standards.

headline: VA Rescinds 2018 Directive on Transgender Treatments, Aligning with Trump's Two-Sexes EO
summary: The VA rescinded its 2018 directive providing hormone therapy and other transgender-related medical services to new patients, aligning with Trump's executive order on sex and gender; veterans already receiving hormone therapy retained coverage.
credibility_rationale: Major national outlet, though its politics desk is frequently characterized as ideologically aligned with the administration on this topic.

headline: Trump Orders Withdrawal From Global Tax Deal And Initiates America First Trade Policy
summary: On his first day in office Trump signed a memorandum declaring that OECD global minimum tax commitments made by the Biden administration "have no force or effect" in the U.S. absent congressional action, and suspended U.S. participation in Pillar One negotiations.
credibility_rationale: Forbes contributor piece citing the official memorandum; not a wire service but widely corroborated.

headline: DOGE proposes cutting IRS workforce by a total of nearly 20%
summary: The Trump administration and DOGE moved to cut the IRS workforce by roughly 20%, on top of earlier layoffs of probationary employees and buyouts, going well beyond the Treasury chapter's call to merely hold the IRS budget flat.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards reporting on internal agency planning documents.

headline: The IRS has lost almost one-third of its tax auditors after 2 months of DOGE cuts, report says
summary: An internal watchdog report found the IRS lost roughly 31% of its tax auditors within two months of DOGE-driven cuts, part of a broader downsizing that also cut about 40% of the IT workforce during 2025.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet reporting based on an internal Treasury/IRS watchdog report.

headline: Trump administration warms to IMF and World Bank, in rare nod to global bodies
summary: After a February 2025 executive order triggered a six-month review of U.S. membership in international bodies including the IMF and World Bank, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent by 2026 had shifted toward working with both institutions rather than pursuing withdrawal.
credibility_rationale: Major regional newspaper with editorial standards.

headline: President Trump Announces "America First Investment Policy" to Promote Investments from Allies and Enhance Restrictions on China
summary: A February 2025 White House policy memo directed tighter CFIUS scrutiny of Chinese investment, including a push to expand CFIUS jurisdiction to cover greenfield investments, though no legislation making Defense a formal CFIUS co-chair has passed.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client alert summarizing an official White House policy document.

headline: Trump is planning a massive IPO of the government's mortgage companies
summary: The administration said it was planning a partial public stock offering of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac that could raise around $30 billion, a step toward privatization, while the companies would remain under conservatorship and government oversight.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Privatizing Fannie Mae is risky. Would it be a win for taxpayers or Trump's donors?
summary: As of February 2026, FHFA Director Bill Pulte said a decision on the Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac IPO plan was still pending, with the companies remaining in conservatorship more than a year after the administration first floated privatization.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards.

headline: U.S. Department of the Treasury Announces Publication of Interim Final Rule Removing Reporting Requirements for U.S. Companies and U.S. Persons
summary: FinCEN issued an interim final rule exempting all U.S.-formed companies and persons from Corporate Transparency Act beneficial ownership reporting, narrowing the rule to apply only to foreign entities registered to do business in the U.S.
credibility_rationale: Official government press release and rule announcement.

headline: President Trump Acts to Roll Back DEI Initiatives
source: Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance
summary: Executive orders signed in January 2025 directed all federal agencies, including Treasury, to close DEI offices and place staff on leave as part of a government-wide rollback of diversity, equity and inclusion programs.
credibility_rationale: Academic law-school governance forum summarizing official executive orders.

headline: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Closes De Minimis Exemptions to Combat China's Role in America's Synthetic Opioid Crisis
summary: An April 2025 executive order ended duty-free de minimis treatment for low-value shipments from China and Hong Kong effective May 2, 2025; a July 2025 order later extended the elimination of the $800 de minimis exemption globally.
credibility_rationale: Official White House fact sheet describing a signed executive order.

headline: Brookings experts on the Supreme Court's tariff decision
summary: The Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Learning Resources v. Trump that IEEPA does not authorize the sweeping reciprocal and China/Mexico/Canada tariffs Trump imposed, forcing the administration to halt IEEPA tariff collection and pivot to Section 301 and 232 authorities instead.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan think tank analysis of an official Supreme Court ruling.

headline: Proposed New Section 301 Tariffs and Other Trade-Related Developments
summary: Following the Supreme Court's invalidation of IEEPA tariffs, the administration launched new Section 301 investigations covering manufacturing overcapacity and forced labor across dozens of countries, expanding rather than repealing Section 232/301 tariff authority as the free-trade essay recommended.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client alert tracking official USTR notices and investigations.

headline: Trump signs executive order on TikTok deal: what to know
summary: Rather than banning TikTok as Project 2025 recommended, Trump signed an executive order advancing a joint-venture deal in which ByteDance's stake falls below 20% and Oracle oversees U.S. data and code, with enforcement paused through January 23, 2026.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards.

headline: Saving TikTok While Protecting National Security
summary: The official executive order framework keeps TikTok operating in the U.S. under restructured, majority-American ownership rather than imposing the outright ban recommended in Project 2025's trade and FCC chapters.
credibility_rationale: Official White House presidential action text.

headline: Export-Import Bank Reauthorization Act of 2026 (S.3772)
summary: Rather than abolishing EXIM or letting its charter lapse at the end of 2026, Congress introduced legislation to extend the bank's charter by another ten years, running contrary to the abolish- and let-lapse recommendations in the Economy chapter.
credibility_rationale: Official congressional legislative record.

headline: President Trump signs Executive Order on Digital Assets and American Financial Technology
summary: Trump signed an executive order on January 23, 2025 prohibiting federal agencies from establishing, issuing, or promoting a U.S. central bank digital currency and directing termination of any ongoing CBDC-related initiatives.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client alert summarizing the official executive order text.

headline: Lee Introduces Bill Making Trump Ban on Central Bank Digital Currency Permanent
summary: Sen. Mike Lee introduced legislation to codify Trump's executive order banning a U.S. central bank digital currency into permanent law, since an executive order alone could be reversed by a future administration.
credibility_rationale: Official congressional office press release describing introduced legislation, though inherently promotional of the sponsor's own bill.

headline: Supreme Court rules Trump cannot fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook for now
summary: In a 5-4 ruling, the Supreme Court blocked Trump's August 2025 attempt to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook while litigation continues, with the majority opinion emphasizing that both the fact and appearance of Federal Reserve independence are central to its design.
credibility_rationale: Major outlet with editorial standards reporting on an official Supreme Court decision.

headline: American Leadership in the Digital Finance Revolution
summary: SEC Chairman Paul Atkins announced "Project Crypto," directing SEC staff to draft simplified rules for digital asset distribution, custody, and trading and declaring that most crypto assets fall outside securities law, with formal rule proposals expected in 2026.
credibility_rationale: Official SEC speech published on the agency's own website.

headline: Trump Administration Seeks to Dismantle CFPB Amid Legal Challenges
summary: Acting CFPB Director Russell Vought ordered a halt to nearly all agency supervision, enforcement, and rulemaking activity in February 2025, prompting a federal judge to issue a preliminary injunction in March 2025 blocking the agency's dismantlement.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client alert summarizing official agency actions and a federal court order.

headline: Warren Statement on Second Court Ruling That Vought Cannot Starve CFPB of Funding
summary: A federal court again rejected Acting Director Vought's attempt to defund the CFPB in early 2026, ruling he could not effectively close the congressionally-created agency without an act of Congress; the underlying litigation continued.
credibility_rationale: Partisan senator's office statement, though it references an official court ruling.

headline: Lawmakers introduce bill to repeal Section 1071 data collection
summary: House and Senate Republicans introduced companion bills to repeal Dodd-Frank Section 1071's small-business lending data collection mandate, though the legislation had not been enacted as of mid-2026.
credibility_rationale: Banking industry trade press with editorial standards.

headline: Is Section 230 Going to Change? The FTC, DOJ and FCC Signal Significant Change for Online Businesses
summary: In April 2025, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr joined DOJ and FTC officials in publicly endorsing a narrower reading of Section 230 that would strip immunity for platform content-removal decisions, though no final FCC order adopting that interpretation had issued as of mid-2026.
credibility_rationale: Law firm client alert summarizing public statements by agency officials.

headline: FTC Has the Resources to Take On Big Tech, Chairman Andrew Ferguson Says
summary: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said Big Tech enforcement remained a top agency priority and that the FTC was proceeding toward trial in its case seeking to break up Meta, continuing antitrust action against dominant internet platforms.
credibility_rationale: Bloomberg wire-quality financial reporting.

headline: Trump Nominates Two Republicans to FEC, Paving Path to End Monthslong 'Shutdown'
summary: The FEC lost its policymaking quorum after commissioner departures beginning in 2025, including one whom Trump attempted to remove; in February 2026 Trump nominated two new commissioners whose confirmation would restore a working quorum.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan nonprofit newsroom with editorial standards.

headline: Trump Has Kneecapped the FEC and Won't Fix It
summary: Following Trump's January 2025 letter purporting to remove Commissioner Ellen Weintraub and further resignations, the FEC dropped to two sitting commissioners by October 2025, leaving it unable to issue rules, advisory opinions, or enforcement decisions.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan nonprofit newsroom with editorial standards.

headline: SBA freezes over 100,000 California borrowers in sweeping $9B pandemic fraud crackdown
summary: SBA Administrator Kelly Loeffler said the agency suspended more than 111,000 California borrowers linked to over $8.6 billion in suspected pandemic-era PPP and EIDL loan fraud as part of a broader nationwide crackdown.
credibility_rationale: Major cable news outlet; coverage aligns with concurrent official SBA releases.

headline: SBA Suspends 7,800 Wisconsin Borrowers Connected to $375 Million in Suspected Fraudulent Pandemic-Era Loans
summary: The SBA announced it had identified and suspended over 150,000 total borrowers connected to more than $10 billion in suspected COVID-era PPP and EIDL fraud as its state-by-state accountability review continued into mid-2026.
credibility_rationale: Official federal agency press release.

headline: Export-Import Bank of the United States: Overview and Reauthorization Issues
summary: The nonpartisan Congressional Research Service reported that EXIM's charter, last extended in 2019 through the end of 2026, faced an active reauthorization debate in the 119th Congress rather than the abolition urged by the Economy chapter's abolish essay.
credibility_rationale: Nonpartisan official congressional research report.
